proseChanges.summary: **Mail choices and deployment declaration:** installation setup now offers email off, your own provider, or Run Edit Run managed email (`MAIL_MODE=off`, `own`, or `rer`). The release carries the corrected mail declaration: the credential names are `EMAIL_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM`, `MAILGUN_SENDING_KEY` and `MAILGUN_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY`; `MAIL_MODE` is public configuration, as are the provider, key-selector, Mailgun domain and region. Native setup now includes Mailgun, using its domain sending key; receiving needs its separate webhook signing key. An explicit `MAIL_PROVIDER=none` or `disabled` wins over a saved `MAIL_MODE=own`. Mail off withholds sending and webhook credentials, stops connected-mailbox sends and refuses Mailgun forwards; move any live forwarding route before switching off. Saving a key or changing a workspace sender does not enable mail. These native choices are active; managed App settings adoption and live hosted Mailgun deployment/delivery qualification remain separate. **rer 0.2.112:** updates the pinned installer from 0.2.110 and uses its deployment-policy hook to validate the selected mail configuration before mail-secret updates or rotations reach provider work. Cleanup and unrelated secret changes remain possible. Offline deployment previews list proposed public and secret binding names without reading existing remote bindings. No new recovery flow is adopted in this release. **Legacy packages and bounded import:** Move in now accepts a chunked original HappyToHelp export folder, uploads immutable files privately, and runs an explicitly approved, resumable background import with Stop, Resume and reconciliation results. Upload alone imports no history and starts no job. AI usage history is omitted by default. Intake and the runner are active, but source and destination workspace IDs must match: adoption into an arbitrary fresh workspace and ID remapping are not implemented. Real customer remote use remains unqualified because staged-package retention and contact-erasure coverage are incomplete. Work exceeding an indivisible slice limit pauses; stopping preserves already committed history. Imported credentials, pending operations and financial custody keep their existing revoked, held or inert treatment. **Knowledge planning and pending index work:** the background legacy importer now plans copied-text references without writing during planning, then commits references with the admitted imported rows. A pending knowledge index drains one source per continuation while keeping the import cursor, rather than blocking the same slice repeatedly. Imported message and private-note content stays literal; other eligible copied fields match destination knowledge only. This processing is active in the Worker importer; the command-line importer keeps its existing indexing path, and this adds no general backlog drain to ordinary native writes. **Import diagnostics:** authorized owners and admins can read bounded Zendesk ticket/article census pages showing imported-to-native links, missing native records, duplicate mappings and linked message counts. Separate restricted mail diagnostics return counts and categories for a fixed set of synthetic acceptance scenarios. These APIs are active, read-only and permission-controlled; they expose no transcript or article content, request no provider work and add no dashboard screen. The mail diagnostics do not establish live delivery. **Move in after sign-in:** the Business Move in link now continues through password sign-in and required two-factor verification to the original-service export section in the selected workspace. Without a selected workspace it opens Projects; choose or create a workspace and reopen the Business link. This active continuation grants no membership or import permission. **Migrations:** one since v0.4.22: `327_legacy_import_worker.sql`, applied once BEFORE the new Worker serves traffic. Upgrade order is v0.4.22 -> v0.4.23. It is additive: seven private run, part, context, message, media, identity and count tables plus their indexes; no existing rows, identities, permissions or work are rewritten. Applying it starts no import, sends no mail and queues no work. Back up first. A v0.4.21 installation first applies 324 and 325 with their published buyer steps, then 327; 326 remains reserved and has no file in this release. The complete migration inventory is 191 files.
proseChanges.was: v0.4.22 is the upgrade baseline, with 190 migrations and rer 0.2.110.
proseChanges.now: v0.4.23 carries the corrected mail declaration and native mail choice, rer 0.2.112, active bounded matched-workspace legacy imports and knowledge processing, restricted diagnostics and sign-in continuation. It adds migration 327; upgrade baselines are v0.4.22 and v0.4.21. Fresh-workspace adoption and real customer remote importer use remain unqualified.
proseChanges.ownerAction: Update from v0.4.22 without resetting. Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state and private settings first. Use Node 22.20.0, pnpm 10.12.4 and pinned rer 0.2.112. Retain native owners, permissions, support history, files, erasure fences and every applied migration identity. Apply 327_legacy_import_worker.sql once BEFORE the new Worker serves traffic, in upgrade order v0.4.22 -> v0.4.23. A v0.4.21 installation applies 324_scheduler_outbox_reads.sql, then 325_knowledge_documents_version_url.sql, then 327, once each, retaining their published buyer steps; earlier installations first apply every other missing published migration in filename order. There is no migration 326 in this release. Run `rer deploy --dry-run` against the retained installation before any separately authorized deployment. No reset, cutover or production deployment is part of this release. Fresh-workspace importer adoption, recovery adoption and live-provider qualification remain separate.

migrations.buyerSteps: Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state and private settings first. Upgrade v0.4.22 -> v0.4.23: apply 327_legacy_import_worker.sql once after every missing published migration and BEFORE the new Worker serves traffic. A v0.4.21 installation applies 324, then 325 with their published buyer steps, then 327. 326 remains reserved and has no file in this release. Additive only: seven private run/part/context/message/media/identity/count tables and their indexes; no existing rows, identities, permissions or work are changed, and applying this SQL starts no import or other work. No reset. Uploaded package retention and contact-erasure coverage remain unqualified for real customer remote use; matched-workspace import is qualified with local synthetic data only.

pendingMigrations.buyerSteps: Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state and private settings. Apply all missing published migrations in order, then 327 and 328 once BEFORE the v2 Worker serves HTTP or queue traffic. Additive adoption reservations, provenance, explicit historical mapping profile and actor origins; preserves native accounts, setup workspace and Business binding. No reset, mail activation or cutover.

After the same complete backup, apply 329 once after 328 and BEFORE the v2 Worker serves HTTP or queue traffic. Additive private custody, ordinal key ledger, permanent scope fences and retention cleanup indexes. Missing schema refuses source intake. Keep original synthetic v1 sources separate and cleanup-only; do not relabel them v2 or admit real customer sources before independent qualification. No version bump, reset or deployment authorized.

Back up D1, R2, Durable Object state and private settings first. Apply once after 329 and any intervening published migrations (330 is reserved for platform recovery), BEFORE serving this Worker. Additive cleanup-only v1 seed/inventory cursors, completion fences and a private installation baseline table; no account backfill or v1 adoption. Keep the old Worker stopped during upgrade. Old synthetic manifest/prefix coordinates are registered pagewise before bounded purge; erasure remains pending until inventory and seeding complete. No reset or customer enablement.

After the same complete backup, apply once after 331 and BEFORE serving this Worker. Removes only the pristine, unstarted inventory marker when no package custody or import run exists, keeping empty native restore targets empty. Existing cursors and package/run inventory remain intact. Bounded discovery creates missing inventory lazily; missing or incomplete inventory still prevents source-cleanup completion. No source, account or permission changes and no reset.
